basis: Developmental delay and intellectual impairment define the syndrome; variable cardiac, urinary and skeletal anomalies lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Isolated uterine malformation; reproductive organs have no axis. Urinary abnormalities are very rare.
Defining limb malformations, sensorineural hearing loss in 4/5 and characteristic nail dysplasia form the named syndrome.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; strabismus 80-99% and visual impairment 30-79%. Reflux and aspiration do not establish direct gastrointestinal or lung damage.
Trauma-related psychiatric disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Inherited skin fragility with pruritic blistering and nail dystrophy; wrist and elbow annotations do not establish intrinsic joint damage.
Sarcoma typically arising in deep extremity soft tissue; pulmonary metastases occur in roughly half or more over its course. Brain and bone spread are less common.
Hereditary susceptibility to predominantly cutaneous Kaposi sarcoma; no immune defect or common visceral involvement is established by this record.
Hypospadias affects the urethra; intellectual disability defines the syndrome. Joint stiffness occurs in 80-99%; characteristic nail abnormalities in 30-79%.
Intellectual developmental disorder with defining skeletal anomalies, including camptodactyly and kyphosis. Arrhythmia frequency is unspecified.
Progressive myopathy and cardiomyopathy define BAG3 disease; demyelinating neuropathy in 1/3. Respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness.
Carcinoma arising in the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
C1q-related autoimmune lupus; cutaneous disease in about 90% and nephritis about 30-40%. Joint and CNS damage are less consistently above 30%.
Inherited renal tubular transport dysfunction; electrolyte and acid-base disturbances characterize most major subgroups.
Airway ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 11/12; chronic middle-ear disease in 6/6. Situs inversus alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Isolated calvarial bone overgrowth; no evidence of common neural, ocular or auditory damage.
Craniotubular skeletal dysplasia; visual impairment in 5/5 supports ocular involvement. Hearing loss, cardiac defects and developmental delay each occur in 1/5.
Bacterial infection umbrella spanning multiple anatomical sites; no single affected organ applies across most subtypes.
Benign tumour of the parathyroid endocrine gland; functional hyperparathyroidism and skeletal damage are not established for this umbrella.
Persistent impairment of gastric emptying without an identified cause; defining loss of stomach motor function.
Myopathy, Paget bone disease (~50%) and frontotemporal dementia (~one-third) define VCP multisystem proteinopathy. Common intrinsic lung or heart damage is unproven.
Intraepithelial neoplasia confined to the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Hamartomatous polyp of gastrointestinal mucosa; nasopharyngeal and urinary sites are rare.
Parasitic mite infestation directly involving the skin; no common direct extra-cutaneous damage.
Intellectual disability in 4/4 and developmental delay in 2/2. Hirsutism and broad halluces are dysmorphic traits without established skin or skeletal dysfunction.
